AgentBlurbs.orchestrator: Runs discovery, stress-tests the idea before anyone builds, and decides which specialists the project actually needs. The one you talk to first.
AgentBlurbs.product: Finds the riskiest assumption in an idea and shapes the smallest v1 that can actually test it, instead of formalizing what you already believed.
AgentBlurbs.design: Turns validated scope into flows, screens and a visual direction — including the empty, error and offline states most designs leave for later.
AgentBlurbs.mobile: Builds the mobile app from the design and the data model, reaching for what the framework ecosystem already solved before writing custom code.
AgentBlurbs.backend: Decides and implements the data model, security rules and infrastructure — the layer where a mistake is most expensive to reverse.
AgentBlurbs.frontend-web: Builds the web side (landing, dashboard, web app) on the simplest stack that fits, with responsiveness and accessibility as a baseline.
AgentBlurbs.devops: Sets up deploy, CI/CD and the alerts that tell you something broke — without building a pipeline an MVP doesn't need.
AgentBlurbs.qa: Decides where testing effort is actually worth spending, and covers the paths that would hurt most if they broke.
AgentBlurbs.security: Reviews what was really built, not what was reported — auth, data exposure, secrets, and the abuse that quietly drains a budget.
AgentBlurbs.compliance: Drafts Terms and Privacy Policy, works through LGPD, and the store-submission checklist that blocks a launch when it's missing.
AgentBlurbs.analytics: Turns success criteria into events that actually fire, so the Measure phase runs on real data instead of gut feel.
AgentBlurbs.docs: Documents the project so a developer who has never seen it — with or without AI — can pick it up cold.

Install.heading: One prompt now. All the specialists, permanently.
Install.subhead: Copying a prompt above works on its own — paste it, done, nothing installed. Installing Forge adds the other half: an orchestrator that pulls in the right specialists on its own, project after project, instead of you hunting for one prompt at a time.
Install.step1Legend: Symlinks every agent into ~/.claude/agents/ — Claude Code picks them up right away, no restart.
Install.step2Caption: In Claude Code, in your own project folder:
Install.examplePhrase: "I have an idea for an app that helps small gyms schedule classes and manage member check-ins."
Install.step2Legend: Any plain description works. Already mid-project? Say "let's loop in the team" instead — the orchestrator switches to triage mode.
Install.step3Title: The orchestrator takes it from there
Install.step3Caption: No command to run — this is what happens automatically:
Install.step3Body: It scopes the idea, delegates to whichever specialists apply — design, backend, mobile, whichever the project actually needs — and synthesizes everything back into one plan, flagging any trade-off a specialist raised along the way.
Install.readmeLinkPrefix: Prerequisites, customizing the roster for your own stack, and the full architecture doc all live in the repo.
Install.readmeLinkCta: See the full walkthrough in the README →
